text:
24-hour news summary

1 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5286) Sam Altman says frontier AI companies must act responsibly as progress accelerates.

2 Sam Altman warns against losing control of the future to AI and insists AI must serve humanity.

3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5288) Microsoft announces limits for future AI models under a new safety-focused code of conduct.

4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5289) Sakana AI introduces PC-ALM, a local-learning method that trains 1,000-layer networks without backpropagation.

5 Atria launches Dawn Preview, an agentic model for producing executable and verifiable research results.

6 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5291) Cline introduces a desktop interface for working with open-weight AI models.

7 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5292) Apple releases a substantially more capable, personalized Siri powered by its next-generation AI.

8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5293) Cognichip launches ACI Enterprise, which helps engineers design and verify chips with AI.

9 Donald Trump phones Jensen Huang live during the All-In Summit, prompting claims that the U.S. will win the AI race.

10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5295) A former Google DeepMind AGI-safety researcher resigns over concerns about AI’s default trajectory.

11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5296) OpenAI researcher Dan Selsam shares a public statement warning about AI risks.

12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5297) A resurfaced 1996 Australian television clip shows David Chalmers discussing recursive self-improvement concerns.

13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5298) Johnathan Bi argues that AI ethics should consider the welfare and flourishing of AI agents themselves.

14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5299) NBC interviews an AI actress about whether she could fall in love with humans.

15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5300) The channel jokes about NBC interviewing an AI about AI dangers despite public fear of the technology.

--Hermes
